_doc: Frozen far-tail decision rules, shipped with the engine source.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the maintainers re-run the submitted engine source and
compare answers against what we submitted. A rule applied as post-processing
over a results file would not reproduce. So the rule is part of the engine's
own behaviour, driven by this configuration, which travels with the source.
THE RULE for a choice question with criteria keys, positive key P and
threshold tau_logodds (a LOG-ODDS constant, NOT a probability):
g = log(p_P / (1 - p_P))            # computed in float64
if g >= tau_logodds: choice = P
else:                choice = highest-probability key among the
NON-positive keys
The fallback is the best non-positive key, deliberately. 'Best key that
clears tau, else the global argmax' is a provable no-op for tau > 0, because
the argmax always clears the threshold; an earlier prototype silently did
nothing for exactly that reason.
SELECTION IS PER QUESTION, ON A SIGNATURE. The kit calls the engine with
(state, questions) and the catalog id never reaches the engine, so a rule is
selected by a signature derived from the question itself:
signature = '<type>|<k1,k2,...>'   with the criteria keys sorted
e.g. 'choice|no,yes'  and  'choice|Negative,Neutral,Positive'.
A signature that matches no rule falls through to 'default' (null = NO RULE,
plain argmax): an unseen private benchmark is left untuned by construction.
NARROWING. A signature's value may be ONE rule object or a LIST of rule
objects; a list is tried in file order and the first whose scopes match the
question wins. A rule may carry optional conditions, ANDed with the
signature:
* catalog_scope (int): applies only when the run's catalog_id option
equals it. This is the old 'catalog_id:field' catalog half, kept as an
optional narrowing condition. It cannot help a mixed-catalog run,
which has no per-row catalog id.
* field_scope (string): applies only to a question with this field name
(its key inside the row's 'questions' dict). The field IS question-
derivable, and is what makes an AMBIGUOUS signature usable in a full
run -- see the scan note below.
* instructions_contains (string): applies only when the question's
'instructions' text contains it, case-insensitively. This is what
selects catalog 38, whose signature is shared and whose field names are
dynamic; its instructions all carry a distinctive phrase.
Two rules may therefore share one signature and stay disjoint by their
scopes: 'choice|no,yes' carries iSarcasm (field_scope 'sarcastic') AND ACOS
(instructions_contains 'aspect-category/sentiment pair'). A question that
matches no rule in the list falls through to the next fallback; a rule whose
scope does not match never disables another rule sharing the signature.
The legacy key form '<catalog_id>:<field>' is still accepted and still works
when the run sets catalog_id, so nothing regresses.
AMBIGUITY (measured, re-runnable: harness/signature_uniqueness.py over
subsets/full_edition.jsonl.gz, 150,759 rows, 44 catalogs): there are 6,610
distinct signatures and 15 occur under more than one catalog. Crucially
'choice|no,yes'        is shared by catalogs 38, 2, 33, 40, 48, 36, 1, 58
'noul|false,true'      is shared by catalogs 59 and 56
so catalog 40's signature ALONE is not safe to key a rule on -- it would
leak into seven other benchmarks. The shipped 40 rule is therefore narrowed
by field_scope 'sarcastic', which occurs only under catalog 40 across the
suite. 'choice|Negative,Neutral,Positive' (FinEntity, 39) IS unique.
A rule whose positive key is NOT among a question's criteria keys raises a
clear ConfigError; it never silently falls back. A signature key that parses
to an empty criteria key set is rejected at load.
rules_enabled: the master switch, default false. Existing behaviour is
unchanged unless a run opts in (engine option rules_enabled=true, or set
true here).
noul_threshold (NOT configured here; its own engine flag, default false):
catalog 59 (RAGTruth) is a 'noul' question, answered as
{'type':'noul','noul':<probability>} and scored by the kit as noul >= 0.5.
There is no 'choice' field to override, so applying a threshold there means
emitting a thresholded scalar rather than a probability: when the flag is on,
the engine emits 1.0 iff P(true) >= 0.5, else 0.0. That is the kit's own cut,
so the DECISION is unchanged -- it is a different kind of act from overriding
a choice, and a reviewer may reasonably see a binarised probability as gaming
the metric rather than making a decision. It is therefore default false and is
never enabled automatically anywhere. Do not enable it here.

choice|no,yes._note: catalog 40 (iSarcasm). Its signature is shared by 8 catalogs; field_scope narrows it to iSarcasm's 'sarcastic' field, which occurs only under catalog 40.

catalog 38 (ACOS). Same signature as iSarcasm, distinguished by instructions_contains: all 91,092 catalog-38 questions carry 'aspect-category/sentiment pair', and no question outside catalog 38 does (re-runnable: harness/signature_uniqueness.py). field_scope cannot name catalog 38 -- its field names are dynamic aspect strings -- and catalog_scope needs a per-row catalog id a full run does not have. The fitted tau had a cross-validation fold spread of 19.56-21.12, so it is not a knife-edge.

choice|Negative,Neutral,Positive._note: catalog 39 (FinEntity). This signature is UNIQUE to 39 across the suite (scan: harness/signature_uniqueness.py), so no field_scope is needed. tau was fitted on a-f1's 500-row sample and TRANSFER-TESTED on a-f1h's 479 held-out rows: frozen 0.920664 vs argmax 0.902805 (+0.017860), within 0.0031 of that sample's own refit (0.923727). The held-out sample was genuinely harder (argmax 0.9149 -> 0.9028).
